issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect Developer.attend to have a single parameter attend(course: Course?). The template declares this signature (extension Developer { func attend(course: Course?) { } }). However, the solution implements a different signature (func attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool)) and thus deviates from the specified API. Worse, the solution's Client calls myself.attend(course: swiftCourse) (single-argument call) while Developer.attend in the solution requires two arguments — this makes the solution repository internally inconsistent and would not compile. This mismatch between problem/template and solution will confuse students about the expected method signature and prevents the provided solution from building as-is.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Developer.attend method signature consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: change the solution implementation to the single-parameter form used by the problem and template: func attend(course: Course?) { ... } and implement the intended logic (optional binding, check lowercase name contains "swift", update monthsOfSwiftExperience, and print the participation message). This will align solution code with the problem statement and template and make the provided Client calls compile. Alternatively, if the extra parameter forCredit was intentional, update the problem statement, the template, and all client calls to use the two-parameter signature consistently.

issues.description: The Developer.attend method is specified in the problem statement and the template with the signature attend(course: Course?). However, the solution implementation changes the API to attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool) — adding a new parameter name and arity. This creates a mismatch across artifacts: students reading the problem and using the template will implement or call attend(course:), but the solution declares a different signature (and therefore would not be a drop-in reference). This inconsistency adds needless cognitive load and can cause confusion or compilation errors when mapping the required behavior to the solution code.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution's method signature with the problem and template. Either (a) remove the extra parameter so the solution implements func attend(course: Course?) { ... }, or (b) make the extra parameter optional by providing a default (e.g. func attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool = true) { ... }) so calls using attend(course:) continue to work. Preferred fix: remove the additional parameter to exactly match the specified API and avoid confusing students.
